brief: TURING GARDEN: Gray-Scott reaction-diffusion running on the GPU (WebGL2 with float or half-float render targets and ping-pong framebuffers; detect EXT_color_buffer_float / EXT_color_buffer_half_float and fall back to a CPU simulation at lower resolution when no float render target exists). Many simulation steps per frame (8-24). Paint with the pointer to inject chemical V; Shift or right-drag erases. Render with relief lighting (normals from the V gradient, a light direction the user can move) and selectable palettes (for example coral reef, ink, bioluminescent, ceramic glaze). Signature feature: an interactive (F, k) parameter map, a small 2D chart of feed rate F against kill rate k where the user clicks or drags a crosshair to pick parameters, with named regions using Pearson's 1993 Greek-letter classes plus friendly names (mitosis, coral growth, worms, maze, holes, chaos, moving spots, spots). Only use parameter values you are confident are correct for your diffusion convention (for Du=1.0, Dv=0.5 with a 9-point Laplacian and dt=1, well-known values are mitosis F=0.0367 k=0.0649, coral F=0.0545 k=0.062), keep the convention consistent with your Laplacian and time step, and verify each named preset actually produces its pattern in the harness. Also a parameter-sweep mode where F varies along x and k along y, showing the whole zoo at once. Brush size, speed, pause, clear, Seed random spots. Downloads are blocked, so no save-image button. The first frame must already show grown patterns (pre-run several hundred steps before first display).
